notes:
Independent check. I re-fetched all 12 raw texts from SOURCES.json with curl into review/AF/raw. The 11 archive.org files are byte-identical to the drafter's copies. For newadvent 01075e I stripped the tags and unescaped the entities myself. check_draft.py run against my own fetch: 172 quotes, 97 paragraphs, 0 lines printed (no QUOTE-MISS, no READ-FAIL). That covers every fact-table quote and every link quote, including the Library quotes (Alvares, Budge 1898 and 1928, Lopes, Carli, Cavazzi, Ludolf, La Trobe) at their lines. The voices fields hold no quotes. Beyond string matching, I read about 20 quotes in context to check that the sentence built on them is fair: Bruce vol. 2 on the council and the stoning; Gobat on 1826, 26 Feb 1830, and the Coptic patriarch's decision accepted by Guebra Messih, which 'settled the question'; Butcher on Hassan Pasha, al-Jawhari and Athanasius; McCarter on van Arckel, the 1824 synod, 1835, the Synodical Commission and Andrew Murray jun.; Chalmers on Ntsikana, the Glasgow Society and Soga's 1861 letter; Philip; the Catholic Encyclopedia on 1752, 1846 and 1889. Only Philip (S10) and the 1752 framing (S4) failed this reading. A simulated AF-only merge into a scratch census passes tools/validate-census.mjs (0 data errors).

Rulings on the HANDOVER flags:
(1) AF-1 and AF-2 living by carrier: right. They are on 'continued as' lines whose neighbors P2-V already carries by the same entries, IX.20 and IX.10. Both carriers hold their own CR evidence and are not carried, so the validator passes. Only the descent grades are inconsistent (M8).
(2) AF-3 living with grade none, VI.13a repointed, and VI.13's carrier swap. Under P2-V as ruled (G-5 a; CO-3: no recorded end and no dated source stays living, graded none, source wanted), AF-3 is rightly living. It does not meet R2-R3 on dated evidence, and neither did VI.13a, whose mark P2-V reviewed and approved. AF-3 ending in the 1880s does not matter: the mark belongs to the tradition, not to the entry's dates. Moving the mark to the latest entry is P2-V's own pattern, and the VI.13 swap is the smallest change the validator allows. Do not re-route the mark through IX.59. What needs fixing is the basis wording and the wanted source (S2), and treating AF-4 and AF-5 the same way (S1). If the coordinator instead reads Review_Brief's line strictly ('only with R2 to R4 evidence'), then AF-3 goes to false, VI.13a keeps its own grade, VI.13 is left alone, and VI.13a's basis is changed to name the gap after 1881. That would contradict P2-V's approved handling of VI.13a, so I do not recommend it.
(3) The added Catholic Encyclopedia 'Abyssinia' source is acceptable. It is public domain, opened raw, flagged, and its stance is stated in the prose ('These accounts are Catholic'; 'a Catholic account, not the church's own'). Fixes needed: the 1752 framing (S4), the de Jacobis spelling (M1) and the sourcing line (M4).
(4) Empty modernCountries for AF-3 to AF-5: correct under the rules. Fill the IDs at apply after a Wikidata lookup (M7).
(5) AF-2 in era 8 with start 1517: approve. Mark's leave covers the start. G89-6 sub-question 2 (i) lets a new row cross an era line. Most of the row's span lies in era 8 (133 years in era 7, 165 in era 8, 39 in era 9). Era 7 would break the validator's adjacent-era rule for continuesAs to VIII.13. The statusDescription says plainly that the row begins in the era before. The VII.32 precedent fits.
(6) The DMR grades on IV.26 -> AF-2 and AF-2 -> VIII.13: approve. Both rest on Budge's 1928 compiled list (a secondary in the Library, verified-direct), with Meinardus 1999 and Guirguis 2011 as the modern studies the repo cites, which is the DMR definition in the lineage brief. They match the grade of the retired link. AF-2 -> VIII.13 could reach Widely Accepted if Lane's primary were attached; that would be stronger, but the present grade is not wrong. Retiring IV.26 -> VIII.13 is exactly what G89-8 and G89-6 name.
(7) The AF-1 <-> AF-2 'in contact with' link, major by its outcome: approve. The outcome rests on an institutional act shown in the link's own quotes: the Coptic patriarch's decision was brought to Tigray and the dispute was adjusted. Gobat's context, read fresh, says the credentials were 'accepted by the latter, settled the question'. Widely Accepted with verified-online is within the cap. There is precedent in IV.26 <-> Zagwe (the abun outcome).
(8) Frozen rows changed beyond the ruled lines: only the consequential living changes on VI.13a and VI.13 and VI.13a's continuesAs (M11). VIII.49's frozen paragraph is unchanged, and VI.25 gets only the ruled continuesAs.
(9) RV-B's AF-2 -> VII.4 link (the-coptic-church-under-the-ottomans--the-moravian-church-at-herrnhut). AF-2's own text does not support it: AF-2 never names the Moravians, Hooker or Cairo's Brethren, and AF's raw texts do not include Watson. The link does not need AF-2's text, though. The two-way check runs from prose to link, and the link rests on its own quotes (La Trobe 1771, a Library primary; Watson online) and on VII.4's new Cairo line. Its endpoint is right: 1752 falls inside AF-2 (1517-1854) and before VIII.13 starts. Widely Accepted with verified-online is within the cap. Keep it in RV-B only; AF drafts no copy, and none was found. If the coordinator wants the relation visible from the Coptic side, RV-B could add one sourced sentence to AF-2's relationsSummary, but that is optional.

Prose: readable, attributed sentence by sentence, with each source's stance named (Volney hostile, McCarter friendly, the Catholic Encyclopedia Catholic, Bentley partisan). I found no AI tells. The 'X says ... He adds' chains are the cost of honest attribution, not filler. The period slur stays in the fact-table quotes only, as the record directs. Round 2 should be a targeted recheck of S1 to S11 and any new links (S3).
